invariants.rationale: The method accesses attributes and children of 'element', so 'element' must not be null at method exit.
'objects' has methods called on it and an object is added to it, indicating it cannot be null.
List sizes in Java are always non-negative; object is potentially added so size is at least zero.
'heightInPixels' is subtracted to compute coordinates, likely representing a dimension and thus non-negative.
'map' is dereferenced and its methods/fields are used in the method, so it must not be null.
